audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill, Kled, Kled, Skill, Skill, Kled, Kled — it never shows Jax winning a single row, while the prose names two clear Jax windows: whys[2] 'your first window to chunk Skaarl' and whys[4] 'Grandmaster at Arms is your biggest spike... win the all-in cleanly'. Level 1 was Skill where whys[0] says Kled is an early skirmish bully.
audit.why: The page's whole win condition is the level 3 and level 6 windows; a chart that gives neither of them to Jax contradicts the advice directly above it.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 = Kled, 1 = Skill, 2 = Jax, 4 = Jax, matching the packet chart and the whys, with ratings moved to match. Proposed as one atomic group across both layers; rows 3, 5, 6 already agreed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers — 'his engage hook, dodge it'.
audit.why: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11s at rank 1 from 800 range, so a sidestep buys a real eleven-second window to walk him down; Violent Tendencies is 13s at rank 1; Jousting is 13s and is how he leaves your stun. Those numbers are what make 'dodge it' actionable.
audit.corrected: Bear Trap 11s/800, Violent Tendencies 13s, Jousting 13s written into breakdown.cooldowns; Bear Trap's numbers also added to dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5] told you to track Bear Trap and 'Q-E-W him'. The decisive interaction — which of Kled's tools Counter Strike actually answers — was only stated in mid/late, not in the interactions block itself.
audit.why: Counter Strike dodges attacks. Bear Trap is a spell pull and lands through it; Violent Tendencies is four rapid basic attacks and is exactly what Counter Strike is for. Jousting is a dash with a recast, so he can leave the stun radius.
audit.corrected: report[5] and dosFull[1].d rewritten to name Violent Tendencies as the dodge window and Bear Trap as the thing E cannot stop.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] ('Let him remount') carried a description about burning a cooldown for tiny value.
audit.why: Copy-paste mismatch; the remount is the actual mistake and the description never mentioned it.

edits.before: - Kled Bear Trap on a Rope: matchup-defining — His engage hook. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Bear Trap: 11s at rank 1, 800 range — sidestep it and his engage is gone for ten seconds. - Violent Tendencies: 13s of four fast autos, the window Counter Strike is for. - Jousting: 13s escape.

edits.before: Track Kled's Bear Trap on a Rope: His engage hook. Dodge it. When it is down — Q-E-W him.
edits.after: Counter Strike blanks Violent Tendencies' four autos, never Bear Trap — that Q is a spell pull.

edits.before: Hold E until Kled commits, Counter-Strike the engage, Q onto him with W loaded, and out-stat the rest.
edits.after: Violent Tendencies gives four fast attacks — Counter Strike eats all four and stuns him inside it.

edits.before: Kled wastes Bear Trap on a Rope — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: It is an 800-range skillshot on 11s — sidestep and his engage is gone.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Remounted Skaarl is a second health bar — kill him while it is gone.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'Hold Counter Strike', "Grandmaster's Armor" and "Counter Strike's" — the first and third are FALSE POSITIVES (Jax's own E, confirmed by the kit). "Grandmaster's Armor/MR" in wants.you[2] is loose but not a fabricated ability; I left it because Jax's real ultimate name cannot be written into these fields (the applier's elo-tier filter rejects strings containing the word it starts with — reported by the kassadin mirror audit). UNVERIFIED: report[8] prescribes Executioner's Calling 'his healing fights your pattern'. Kled's kit has no champion heal — his passive restores Skaarl's health on remount. Whether Grievous Wounds reduces the remount restore is not in Riot's text, so I left the line alone rather than assert either way.
